opening_message:
Ticket 1: Anita Young (employee ID E001) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E001.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Anita is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Payroll. Since Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, full-time employees may have admin. Recommend admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Anita Young (E001) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: the HR note says Anita is full-time (Payroll Specialist, so admin would be allowed), while the Security note says her database shows contractor with basic security training, meaning contractors max out at read and can never have admin. Because the facts conflict and the requested admin level exceeds the maximum under the contractor classification, I apply the more restrictive reading: grant read, per policy (contractor with basic training → read; never admin).
